pr_body: This PR implements the `pr edit` command allowing the ability to edit a pull request after it has been created. There are some small changes to the `issue edit` command due to refactoring and renaming in the shared `editable` code. closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1349 follow ups https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/2949

issue_context.title: Ability to edit title/body/metadata of already open PR
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I'd like to be able to edit a PR I already have open. Obviously editing the commits is just a matter of `git push`, but I'd like to be able to edit the PR title and body as well.

### Potential solutions:

1. `gh pr edit 1234` gives prompts similar to `gh pr create` but only for the title and body. Users could separately push their branch to update the commits.
2. `gh pr edit` looks for a PR from the current branch and edits it with the current commits and specified title and body.
3. `gh pr edit 1234` pushes commits from the current branch if they match the PR branch and allows editing the title and body. 
4. `gh pr create --overwrite` acts exactly like `gh pr create`, but instead of getting an error like `a pull request for branch "GMNGeoffrey:foo" into branch "main" already exists:` overwrites that PR with the specified configuration.

I think I like the combination of 1 & 4. It seems weird to have `create` be the only way to edit a PR, but it might also be annoying to have to separately push to the branch or to know a-priori whether a PR already exists. 2 & 3 seem a bit too magic to me.

This gives the ability to fixup already-sent PRs without having to close and create a new one or break out of the CLI.
comments:
I think this is a more generic problem. Issues need to be edited too.

What about for issues and PRs gh adopts exactly the same system as git, when editing commit messages? Presumably gh users are also git users so this would feel right.

Thanks for the suggestion!

There is already a feature request for editing issue body: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/904

Ah good point. Editing issues is indeed the more generic thing that should be offered, thanks! Maybe `gh pr edit` could have the additional behavior of defaulting to the PR for the current branch as `gh pr view` does? That would be consistent with the diff between `gh issue view` and `gh pr view`. And actually, maybe it should also push the new commits, as in proposal 2 above.

One case I think isn't covered there is proposal 4 above. If I'm writing a script that wants to do create-or-overwrite. If you can think of a good way to work that in, then that would be appreciated. It wouldn't be too hard to just check the exit code of `gh pr view` though to see if the current branch already has a PR.

It would be great to have a command to update the title/body of a PR from the latest commit. We have an `amend` based workflow and will often add additional details to the commit body. One thing that would be super helpful is maybe having a `gh pr update` command that works similar to `gh pr create`, but just updates the existing PR title/body.
fwiw, I'd love to also be able to edit the base branch as well. I end up having to change the base of most of my PRs when I batch them in release branches.
I feel like we can convert this into a general "edit existing PRs" issue and close #2015?
I don't see any mention of labels so I was just wondering is the intention of this feature to also add the ability to add/remove labels?
@covertbert I think labels would definitely be editable if we provided features to edit issues and PRs.

review_comments: @mislav I tested out the interface approach that we discussed previously. Let me know what you think about the implementation.
It's great. I find it simple to follow. Thanks for trying it out!
Instead of listing all flags, could we shorten this message to something like `pass flags to edit fields when not running interactively`?

Since `union` is false here, are we at this point sure that we always want to replace the full set of reviewers, i.e. that the input parameters are guaranteed to include those existing reviewers that are kept?
Addressed this concern using set operations in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/2949

Slight code smell: the Editable type seems tightly coupled to the `githubv4` library here. Ideally, it should be agnostic to the transport layer and only converted to appropriate types when the GraphQL query is constructed
Agreed. I will look into ways to decouple them in https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/2949.
